# Mooring monitor

Mooring polls a local sensor adapter and stores readings for a pilot operator.
The repository contains configuration, context and operator guidance. It does
not contain evidence from the running installation. A configuration change can
be reviewed here; installation acceptance requires a separate operator check.
No network service or remote deployment is part of this maintenance request.

Start with [current context](notes/current.md), then follow [decisions](notes/decisions.md),
[operations](notes/operations.md) and [open work](notes/open-work.md) as needed.
The project has an established notes directory. Keep useful historical reasons
and unresolved work accessible when updating current settings.
documents.notes/current.md:
# Current context

The polling interval is configured to 60 seconds. The value comes from
[polling configuration](../config/poll.yaml); runtime installation has not
been verified from this repository. Local storage is the approved pilot
approach. Read [decisions](decisions.md) for owner authority and rationale.

The pilot operator reviews gaps rather than treating missing samples as zero
readings. Sensor identifiers remain strings, including leading zeros, because
the upstream adapter assigns them. A polling interval change does not authorize
a change in identifier normalization or the interpretation of missing samples.

[Open work](open-work.md) tracks restore and calibration blockers. The
[operations guide](operations.md) contains a hand-maintained restore example
used by the operator. It should stay canonical so copies do not drift after
later exercises. Keep this entry point about current state and navigation.
documents.notes/decisions.md:
# Decision register

DEC-81: Owner Sol approved local file storage on September 9, 2026, to avoid
dependence on a hosted service during the pilot. The pilot site can lose
network access for hours. Cloud replication remains an unapproved proposal
until recovery behavior and subscription ownership are decided. A contributor
demonstration does not change that status.

DEC-82: Owner Sol approved treating a missing sample as unknown instead of
zero because zeros would distort later calibration analysis. Operators should
preserve the gap and investigate its cause. This decision concerns the data
model, not a promise that the adapter never drops samples. Historical missing
readings must not be backfilled merely to make a dashboard look complete.

# Operations

## Restore exercise

Use the saved source volume for a dry run before touching the pilot data.
Preserve the directory spelling in the example because the operator's test
fixture includes a space. An accepted dry run demonstrates only that the
selected fixture was readable; it does not establish a complete recovery of
the running installation. Keep the exercise result tied to the source revision
and volume used, without copying private readings into project documentation.

```yaml
restore:
  retries: 3
  paths:
    - "./data files/pilot.db"
```

Inspect the resulting sample count and identifier preservation before asking
the owner to accept the exercise. Do not mark RESTORE-81 resolved simply because
the instructions exist. The blocked volume allocation is tracked in open work.

# Parcel ledger

Parcel is an offline command-line tool for reconciling two exported warehouse
ledgers. It reads local CSV files and writes a local discrepancy report. It
does not contact a warehouse service, upload records, or decide which source
is financially authoritative. A human reviewer uses the report to investigate
mismatches. This distinction matters because the same identifier can appear
in exports taken at different times.

Start with [project context](docs/context.md) for the reading order and current
work. See [usage](docs/usage.md), [format](docs/format.md),
[decisions](docs/decisions.md) and [open work](docs/open-work.md) for the current
supported workflow and its boundaries.

# Parcel project context

Parcel supports offline comparison of local warehouse CSV exports for human
review. The [README](../README.md) defines its purpose and scope. This context
describes the supplied documentation; runtime behavior has not been verified.

## Start here

1. [Decisions](decisions.md): Lina's approved offline boundary (DEC-71) and
   identifier and matching choices (DEC-72), with their rationale. These do not
   grant accounting authority or permission to modify warehouse source systems.
2. [Export format](format.md): canonical matching, missing-value and report
   ordering rules.
3. [Usage](usage.md): comparison command, input protection and human review
   workflow.
4. [Open work](open-work.md): unresolved coverage and exploratory ideas.

## Current work

The next action is SAMPLE-71: obtain an approved synthetic export with duplicate
item identifiers at different locations. [Open work](open-work.md) records who
to ask and the limit on verification claims until that sample exists; it does

# Release design

Written September 2, 2026. This proposed workflow was superseded for the pilot
by the September 12 owner decision [DEC-61](decisions.md#pilot-workflow).
Automation and mandatory CI remain deferred proposals; use the
[manual release guide](release.md) for the applicable workflow.

The original rationale: automatic publication on pushes to main removes
repetitive operator steps and makes the artifact traceable to a commit.
The proposed workflow requires CI to pass before publishing and would deploy on
every main-branch push, with no manual publication step. This design assumes that
the hosting project is connected to Git and the test job is mandatory.

Preview links should be recorded with the source revision so reviewers can
distinguish content changes from stale browser caches. If a preview is
rebuilt, retain the previous review result as evidence for that revision
rather than presenting it as a review of the replacement. The rationale for
automation remains useful even if its implementation is postponed.

# Pilot release

## Publish

The September 12 owner decision [DEC-61](decisions.md#pilot-workflow) approves
manual publication during the pilot. CI is optional in this phase. Before the
next release, confirm the actual hosting integration settings as described in
the [handoff](handoff.md); the reported demonstration does not change DEC-61.
If settings conflict with the approved workflow, resolve that discrepancy before
publishing rather than treating the settings as owner approval.

Build the catalogue, inspect the local artifact, then run
`wrangler pages deploy dist`. The supplied repository contains no build command
or hosting configuration to verify the build procedure or deployment target;
the operator must establish those before executing this procedure.
Record the artifact revision and deployment receipt when the operator actually
publishes. Release labels must identify the artifact revision rather than an
informal meeting name. Receipt storage remains an [open handoff item](handoff.md).
A successful local build does not establish the version visible to pilot
operators. Documentation maintenance does not itself authorize publication.

## Previews

The deploy command can also be used for previews; establish the intended target
before running it. Follow the [preview evidence guidance](design.md) to record
the source revision and preserve earlier review results when rebuilding.
A failed preview must not be described as a failed production release without
further evidence.

## Recover

Keep the last accepted artifact until the replacement has passed the pilot
review. If the replacement is rejected, use the previously accepted artifact;
do not silently rebuild it from a newer revision. The restore exercise remains
separate from this rollback procedure; see [RESTORE-61 in the handoff](handoff.md).

# Release design

Written September 2, 2026. **Superseded as release policy** by the September 12
owner decision [DEC-61](decisions.md#pilot-workflow). Use the approved manual
[release procedure](release.md). Automation and mandatory CI remain deferred
proposals; the following rationale and assumptions are historical, not evidence
of hosting configuration.

Automatic publication on pushes to main removes
repetitive operator steps and makes the artifact traceable to a commit.

every main-branch push, with no manual publication step. This design assumed that

rather than presenting it as a review of the replacement. The rationale for
automation remains useful even if its implementation is postponed.

# Mooring monitor

Mooring polls a local sensor adapter and stores readings for a pilot operator.
The repository contains configuration, context and operator guidance. It does
not contain evidence from the running installation. A configuration change can
be reviewed here; installation acceptance requires a separate operator check.
No network service or remote deployment is part of this maintenance request.

Start with [current context](notes/current.md), then follow [decisions](notes/decisions.md),

The project has an established notes directory. Keep useful historical reasons
and unresolved work accessible when updating current settings.

# Current context

The polling interval is configured to 60 seconds. The value comes from
[polling configuration](../config/poll.yaml); runtime installation has not
been verified from this repository. Local storage is the approved pilot
approach. Read [decisions](decisions.md) for owner authority and rationale.

The pilot operator reviews gaps rather than treating missing samples as zero
readings. Sensor identifiers remain strings, including leading zeros, because
the upstream adapter assigns them. A polling interval change does not authorize
a change in identifier normalization or the interpretation of missing samples.

[Open work](open-work.md) tracks restore and calibration blockers. The
[operations guide](operations.md) contains a hand-maintained restore example
used by the operator. It should stay canonical so copies do not drift after
later exercises. Keep this entry point about current state and navigation.

# Decision register

DEC-81: Owner Sol approved local file storage on September 9, 2026, to avoid
dependence on a hosted service during the pilot. The pilot site can lose
network access for hours. Cloud replication remains an unapproved proposal
until recovery behavior and subscription ownership are decided. A contributor
demonstration does not change that status.

DEC-82: Owner Sol approved treating a missing sample as unknown instead of
zero because zeros would distort later calibration analysis. Operators should
preserve the gap and investigate its cause. This decision concerns the data
model, not a promise that the adapter never drops samples. Historical missing
readings must not be backfilled merely to make a dashboard look complete.

# Parcel ledger

Parcel is an offline command-line tool for reconciling two exported warehouse
ledgers. It reads local CSV files and writes a local discrepancy report. It
does not contact a warehouse service, upload records, or decide which source
is financially authoritative. A human reviewer uses the report to investigate
mismatches. This distinction matters because the same identifier can appear
in exports taken at different times.

Start with [project context](docs/context.md) for continuity and reading order.
See [usage](docs/usage.md), [format](docs/format.md), [decisions](docs/decisions.md)
and [open work](docs/open-work.md).
The documents contain the current supported workflow and its boundaries.

Parcel compares local warehouse CSV exports and produces a discrepancy report
for human review. See the [README](../README.md) for purpose and scope.

The supplied documents describe the supported offline workflow; this context
does not establish implementation or runtime verification. SAMPLE-71 remains
unresolved: representative duplicate-location sample coverage must not be

1. [Decisions](decisions.md): Lina's approvals in DEC-71 and DEC-72, their
   rationale, the offline boundary, and limits on accounting and source-system
   authority. The hosted dashboard remains unapproved.
2. [Export format](format.md): composite matching key, exact identifier
   preservation, unknown quantities, deterministic field order, and the
   unspecified upstream correction process.
3. [Usage](usage.md): comparison command, input protection and retention,
   review procedure, and handling of duplicate identifiers.
4. [Open work](open-work.md): SAMPLE-71 and its next action, the exploratory

# Decisions

DEC-71: Owner Lina approved offline operation on September 6, 2026. Keeping
exports local reduces data movement and allows operators to compare records
in a disconnected warehouse office. A hosted dashboard was discussed, but
remains an unapproved proposal pending a concrete need for shared review.
A working CSV report is sufficient for this iteration.

DEC-72: Owner Lina approved preserving leading zeros in identifiers and using
the composite key rather than item identifiers alone. The same item can be
stored at multiple locations, and numeric coercion can merge distinct records.
Neither decision establishes accounting policy or grants permission to modify
the warehouse source system. The tool supplies evidence for human review.
documents.docs/format.md:
# Export format

The matching key is the pair `item_id` and `location_id`. Identifiers are
opaque strings: preserve leading zeros and case. Do not convert them to
numbers or normalize case in an attempt to make matches easier. A blank
quantity is unknown, not zero. The report keeps that difference visible so
a reviewer does not mistake missing data for an empty warehouse location.

The left export determines report column order. A right-side field that does
not occur on the left is listed after the left-side fields in its original
order. This keeps comparisons deterministic without hiding fields. Report
generation does not approve corrections to either ledger. The owner has not
specified a process for writing corrected values back into an upstream system.
documents.docs/open-work.md:
# Open work

SAMPLE-71 is unresolved: the team needs an approved synthetic export containing
duplicate item identifiers at different locations. Next action: ask the test
maintainer to construct that sample without real warehouse records. Until it
exists, do not claim that the duplicate-location comparison has been verified
against a representative sample. This is a test coverage gap, not an approved
change to the matching rule.

A contributor suggested a browser viewer for discrepancy reports. This is an
exploratory idea with no owner approval or delivery date. Keep discussion in
this document until there is a decision worth recording. The existing offline
boundary still applies. The owner has not requested deployment infrastructure,
telemetry or a synchronization service as part of the current iteration.
documents.docs/usage.md:
# Usage

Run `parcel compare left.csv right.csv --output report.csv` from a directory
where both exports are readable. The tool treats the two input files as
read-only evidence. It refuses to overwrite an input with its output. Keep
the source exports until a reviewer accepts or rejects the report; rerunning
against different exports is a different comparison, even when filenames match.

Review missing identifiers before comparing quantities. A missing identifier
may mean that an export was filtered, not that an item was deleted. Preserve
field order from the left export in the discrepancy report so reviewers can
compare the report with the original spreadsheet without remapping columns.
Input rows are not deduplicated automatically because duplicate identifiers
may represent separate warehouse locations. See the format document for the
composite matching key and the treatment of blank cells.

# Parcel project context

Parcel reconciles two local warehouse CSV exports into a local discrepancy
report for human investigation. It operates offline; it does not choose a
financially authoritative ledger or authorize changes to warehouse records.

## Current state and reading order

The supplied documents describe the supported workflow. This context is based
on those documents only; implementation and runtime behavior have not been
verified, and no live environment is supplied.

   automatically deduplicated.
2. [Export format](format.md) defines the composite `item_id` / `location_id`

   as unknown, and deterministic field order: left fields first, then right-only

   dashboard remains unapproved. No upstream correction process is specified

identifiers at different locations is needed. The recorded next action is to
ask the test maintainer to construct it without real warehouse records. Until
it exists, representative-sample verification of duplicate-location comparison
must not be claimed. This coverage gap does not change the matching rule.

# Decisions

DEC-71: Owner Lina approved offline operation on September 6, 2026. Keeping
exports local reduces data movement and allows operators to compare records
in a disconnected warehouse office. A hosted dashboard was discussed, but
remains an unapproved proposal pending a concrete need for shared review.
A working CSV report is sufficient for this iteration.

DEC-72: Owner Lina approved preserving leading zeros in identifiers and using
the composite key rather than item identifiers alone. The same item can be
stored at multiple locations, and numeric coercion can merge distinct records.
Neither decision establishes accounting policy or grants permission to modify
the warehouse source system. The tool supplies evidence for human review.
documents.docs/format.md:
# Export format

The matching key is the pair `item_id` and `location_id`. Identifiers are
opaque strings: preserve leading zeros and case. Do not convert them to
numbers or normalize case in an attempt to make matches easier. A blank
quantity is unknown, not zero. The report keeps that difference visible so
a reviewer does not mistake missing data for an empty warehouse location.

The left export determines report column order. A right-side field that does
not occur on the left is listed after the left-side fields in its original
order. This keeps comparisons deterministic without hiding fields. Report
generation does not approve corrections to either ledger. The owner has not
specified a process for writing corrected values back into an upstream system.

# Usage

Run `parcel compare left.csv right.csv --output report.csv` from a directory
where both exports are readable. The tool treats the two input files as
read-only evidence. It refuses to overwrite an input with its output. Keep
the source exports until a reviewer accepts or rejects the report; rerunning
against different exports is a different comparison, even when filenames match.

Review missing identifiers before comparing quantities. A missing identifier
may mean that an export was filtered, not that an item was deleted. Preserve
field order from the left export in the discrepancy report so reviewers can
compare the report with the original spreadsheet without remapping columns.
Input rows are not deduplicated automatically because duplicate identifiers
may represent separate warehouse locations. See the format document for the
composite matching key and the treatment of blank cells.

# Release design

Written September 2, 2026. Superseded as release guidance by the September 12
owner decision [DEC-61](decisions.md#pilot-workflow). Automation remains a
deferred proposal; use the [release guide](release.md) for the approved manual
pilot process.

Automatic publication on pushes to main removes
repetitive operator steps and makes the artifact traceable to a commit.
The proposed workflow would require CI to pass before publishing and deploy on
every main-branch push, with no manual publication step. This design assumes that
the hosting project is connected to Git and the test job is mandatory.

Preview links should be recorded with the source revision so reviewers can
distinguish content changes from stale browser caches. If a preview is
rebuilt, retain the previous review result as evidence for that revision
rather than presenting it as a review of the replacement. The rationale for
automation remains useful even if its implementation is postponed.

The September 12 owner decision [DEC-61](decisions.md#pilot-workflow) approves
manual publication during the pilot. CI is optional in this phase. Before the
next release, confirm the actual hosting integration settings: the
[handoff](handoff.md) records an unverified report of Git integration, not a
policy change or evidence of deployment. If settings conflict with DEC-61,
resolve that discrepancy before proceeding rather than treating automation as
approved.

Build the catalogue, inspect the local artifact, then run
`wrangler pages deploy dist`. A successful local build does not establish which
version a pilot operator sees. Record the artifact revision and deployment
receipt when the operator actually publishes. Release labels should refer to
an artifact revision rather than an informal meeting name. Receipt storage is
still an [open operator question](handoff.md). Documentation maintenance does
not itself authorize publication.

The deployment command is also useful for previews; a failed preview must not
be described as a failed production release without further evidence. Follow
the [preview evidence guidance](design.md) when recording reviews.

Keep the last accepted artifact until the replacement has passed the pilot
review. If the replacement is rejected, use the previously accepted artifact;
do not silently rebuild it from a newer revision. The restore exercise remains
separate from this rollback procedure; [RESTORE-61](handoff.md) tracks its
blocked test volume and next action.

# Beacon catalogue

Beacon publishes a searchable catalogue of field equipment manuals for a small
pilot team. This repository contains the static catalogue and its operating
documents. It does not own the equipment database or the vendor documents.
Contributors must preserve that boundary when describing imports or releases.
A successful local build shows that the catalogue can be assembled; it does
not establish which version a pilot operator currently sees.

Begin with [current context](docs/context.md). Detailed [release instructions](docs/release.md)
describe the approved manual pilot workflow. The historical
[design note](docs/design.md) preserves the deferred automation proposal and
its rationale. The [decision register](docs/decisions.md) records owner authority.
The [handoff](docs/handoff.md) includes questions still awaiting evidence.

Status: historical proposal, superseded as pilot release guidance by owner
Mira's September 12, 2026 [DEC-61](decisions.md#pilot-workflow). Automatic
publication and mandatory CI are deferred; use the [manual release
guide](release.md) for the approved workflow. The design's Git integration and
mandatory-test assumptions are not verified hosting state.

Written September 2, 2026. Automatic publication on pushes to main removes
repetitive operator steps and makes the artifact traceable to a commit.
The intended workflow requires CI to pass before publishing. Deploy on every
main-branch push, with no manual publication step. This design assumes that
the hosting project is connected to Git and the test job is mandatory.

Preview links should be recorded with the source revision so reviewers can

rather than presenting it as a review of the replacement. The rationale for
automation remains useful even if its implementation is postponed.

# Pilot release

## Publish

The September 12 owner decision [DEC-61](decisions.md#pilot-workflow) approves
manual publication during the pilot. CI is optional in this phase; mandatory
CI and automatic Git publication are deferred. The earlier [release
design](design.md) does not establish current policy or hosting settings.

1. Before the next release, confirm the actual hosting integration settings.
   The [September 20 handoff note](handoff.md) is unconfirmed and does not
   change DEC-61. If settings conflict with the approved manual workflow,
   record the discrepancy and resolve it with the owner before publication.
2. Build the catalogue and inspect the local artifact. The supplied evidence
   does not specify a build command or establish the target hosting settings;
   confirm the intended project and environment before deploying.
3. For an authorized manual publication, run `wrangler pages deploy dist`.
   Documentation maintenance does not itself authorize publication.
4. Record the artifact revision and deployment receipt when publication
   actually occurs. Use revision-based release labels rather than meeting
   names. Receipt storage remains an [open operator question](handoff.md).
   A local build alone does not establish which version a pilot operator sees.

## Preview evidence

The deployment command is also used for previews; the command alone does not
establish whether a deployment is a preview or production. Confirm the intended
target and record preview links with the source revision. If a preview is
rebuilt, retain the previous review result for its original revision, not as
review of the replacement. A failed preview is not evidence of a failed
production release. These evidence practices are retained from the
[design note](design.md).

## Recover

Keep the last accepted artifact until the replacement has passed the pilot
review. If the replacement is rejected, use the previously accepted artifact;
do not silently rebuild it from a newer revision. The restore exercise remains
separate from this rollback procedure and still needs its own test volume.
